result.title: Spectral Degeneration of Self-Attention under Isotropic Score Geometry
result.summary: We study the spectral structure of the self-attention matrix in Transformer models through an idealized spectral model for the pre-softmax score matrix. Motivated by the rotational isotropy of query and key representations, our model replaces the random token-space orientation of the score matrix by its canonical singular-value representative with a logarithmic spike--bulk separation. Empirical diagnostics on pretrained vision and language transformers motivate this model: token-space singular matrices have nearly uniform eigen-angle distributions, and score spectra are dominated by a small number of effective directions. We then prove that the row-wise softmax map transforms this structure into a degenerate attention matrix: dominant modes are preserved, whereas the bulk spectral distributions concentrate at zero. Stable rank remains bounded for bidirectional attention but grows logarithmically for causal attention. Within the canonical model, these results explain how attention can preserve a small number of dominant directions while compressing the remaining bulk modes.

AI.brief_summary: 论文为 pre-softmax score 矩阵建立理想化谱模型（由 query/key 旋转各向同性假设得到对数 spike–bulk 分离的典型奇异值），并在该模型下证明 row-wise softmax 会把少数主方向保留、把 bulk 谱压向零，同时给出双向注意力 stable rank 有界、因果注意力对数增长的结论。
